statement: If G is a simple connected graph, then L_s(G) ≥ 2(average of λ(v) - 1)

readings.interpretation: L_s >= 2*(avg lambda(v) - 1); lambda(v)=2 all v (glossary: local independence = alpha of G[N(v)])
L_s >= 2*avg(lambda) - 1 (alternate precedence)

notes: Glossary defs: L_s (max leaves over spanning trees; = n - gamma_c = 20-3 = 17, verified: no CDS of size 2, CDS {0,4,8} of size 3); lambda(v) (alpha of induced neighborhood) = 2 for all v by vertex-transitivity.

statement: If G is a simple connected graph, then b(G) ≥ FLOOR(average of ecc(v)+maximum of λ(v))

readings.interpretation: b >= floor(avg ecc + max lambda)
b >= floor(avg ecc) + max lambda (alternate grouping)

notes: Equality case. b=4 verified two ways: exhaustive check found no 5-vertex induced bipartite subgraph (and alpha=2 forces any induced bipartite k-set to have ceil(k/2)<=2 => k<=4); witness {0,1,8,9}. ecc(v)=2 for all v.

statement: If G is a simple connected graph on more than one vertex, then f(G) ≥ CEIL[(p(G)+b(G)+1)/2]

readings.interpretation: f >= ceil((p+b+1)/2); p = path covering number (glossary), G is traceable so p=1

notes: Hamiltonian path verified by search => p=1. f=4 verified: no 5-vertex induced forest exists (exhaustive over C(20,5)); induced tree {0,4,8,12} gives f>=4.

statement: If G is a simple connected graph, then f(G) ≥ CEIL[sqrt[res(G)*b(G)]]

readings.interpretation: f >= ceil(sqrt(residue * b))

notes: Residue independently recomputed by Havel-Hakimi on non-increasing sequence (glossary Note on def 42): final sequence [0,0] => residue 2 (consistent with residue <= alpha = 2).

statement: If G is a simple connected graph, then f(G) ≥ res(G)+ CEIL[diam(G)/3]

readings.interpretation: f >= residue + ceil(diam/3)

notes: Straightforward; residue=2 verified by direct Havel-Hakimi run.

statement: If G is a simple connected graph, then f(G) ≥ CEIL[(minimum of dist_even(v) + b(G) + 1)/3]

readings.interpretation: dist_even(v) counts v itself (glossary: page examples imply v counted): min dist_even = 9
dist_even(v) excludes v: min dist_even = 8

notes: VIOLATED under both dist_even conventions (RHS=5 > f=4 either way). Independently verified: f=4 (exhaustive: no 5-subset induces a forest; alpha=2 argument also caps f at 4 since a k-vertex forest has independent set >= ceil(k/2); induced-tree witness {0,4,8,12}); dist_even(0): distances from v=0 are 0 (self), 1 (11 vertices), 2 (8 vertices in blobs +-2) => 9 with self, 8 without; vertex-transitive so min=max. Bracketing (sum)/3 is explicit in statement_text.

f >= ceil(sqrt(alpha) * (1 + (n mod Delta)))
f >= ceil(sqrt(alpha*1) + (n mod Delta))
